source.title: Interpreting Attention Layer Outputs with Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Connor Kissane; Robert Krzyzanowski; J. Bloom; Arthur Conmy; Neel Nanda

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether omitting SAE reconstruction error affects model behavior, using attention-output SAEs and IOI performance rather than the original study's error-predictability and scaling analyses.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates SAE reconstructions and directly ablates an SAE error term. It does not test linear predictability, error-norm scaling across SAE sizes, comparisons with matched random errors, or whether different SAE training methods remove dark matter.
record.test_reason: A tool paper on attention-output SAEs. In Appendix K it splices SAE reconstructions (dropping the error term) into GPT-2 Small and measures IOI logit difference and KL. It also ablates the error term at layer 5. Both bear directly on V5 in a new setting: attention-output SAEs and the IOI circuit. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but narrow. The paper's main conclusion is that attention-output SAEs give sparse, interpretable decompositions and are useful for circuit analysis. On the error term, the authors find the SAEs adequate for IOI at layers 1–6. They find them insufficient at layer 0 and layers 7–11, so no end-to-end IOI feature circuit was possible. They note the L5 error-term ablation has a minor effect compared with the top features.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains SAEs on concatenated attention-head outputs and evaluates reconstruction substitutions and an IOI error-term ablation; it does not perform the original study's dark-matter predictability or scaling measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction fidelity varies by layer: layers 1–6 are reported as sufficient for IOI analysis, whereas layer 0 and layers 7–8 show notable logit-difference drops and later layers have high KL divergence.
record.problems: The error-term ablation result is narrow: it is reported for layer 5 and the ABBA IOI template. Several reconstruction results are presented only in figures, and the authors note layer-dependent reconstruction limitations.

untested.parts: Linear predictability of the SAE error from the input activation.
Error-norm prediction across SAE sizes; whether larger SAEs fail on the same contexts; whether error vanishes with scale.
No comparison of reconstruction-induced loss with random errors of equal norm.
Linear vs nonlinear error components. The late-layer 'rare name features' explanation is a hypothesis only.
Steering; tasks other than IOI; models other than GPT-2 Small for the behavioural splicing tests.
No comparison of SAE architectures or training objectives on error size.

missing.what: KL divergence between original and SAE-spliced model for each layer and each layer group. The authors use it to judge layers 9–11 broken despite higher logit difference.
Path patching from the S-inhibition head values: the L5 error term gives a logit-difference change of -0.199, ranking 4th among all components.
QK-circuit decomposition: entries involving at least one error term explain about 15% of attention-score variance, versus 62% for 8 feature pairs.

Per-layer cross-entropy loss recovered with the SAE spliced in, relative to zero ablation. It ranges from 75% (Gemma-2B L6) and 76% (GPT-2 L8) to 99% (GPT-2 L0). This is the general cost of dropping the error term, with no random-error control.
missing.versions: V5 (adjacent to V3, which needs a random-error control)

record.verdict_notes: This study predates the original (June 2024 vs Oct 2024), and its error-term analyses are fidelity checks rather than a dark-matter study. Baselines in Figs 14–15 are the clean model and ABC mean ablation; the rows wrongly say 'figure only' for the baseline. Changed tranche from T2 to T3, since the result comes from a new setting (attention-output SAEs on IOI) rather than a method aimed at the original question. Folded the reader's 'challenges' label for r1 into limits_scope, because the absence is layer-dependent.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of SAE error is a linear function of the input activation.
Per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, context overlap across sizes, and whether error vanishes with scale.
The paper does not compare reconstruction-induced loss with random errors of the same size.
Whether linear error contains unlearned features and nonlinear error resists further dictionary learning.
The paper tests reconstruction-only substitutions and one error-term ablation on IOI, not steering or other circuits and behaviors.
No comparison tests whether improved SAE architectures or end-to-end training shrink the error.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Zero-ablated the SAE error term at the S2 position and measured the change in IOI logit difference.
rows.note: The authors describe the error-term ablation as having a minor effect relative to the feature ablations.
rows.check: Value -0.048 is correct, and the top feature gives -0.826. The clean logit difference is not given in text. The same error term gives -0.199 under path patching (Fig 16b), which is not recorded.

source_check.correct: State: partial. Zero-ablating the L5 error term at S2 on ABBA prompts changes logit difference by -0.048; the top feature changes it by -0.826. The authors describe the error effect as minor relative to feature ablations, without establishing that it is negligible or nonsignificant.
source_check.locator_found: Appendix K.1, paragraph preceding Figure 16; Figure 16a.
source_check.problem: A small nonzero effect is partial under the state rules; the paper does not establish absence.

relationships.condition: GPT-2 Small IOI, attention-output SAEs spliced at layer 0 and layers 7–11, singly or as head-class groups
relationships.reason: Dropping the error term causes notable logit-difference drops (layers 0, 7, 8) or high KL (9–11), and the authors deem these SAEs insufficient for circuit analysis (r2, r9, r10, r14, r17, r18). The late-layer KL evidence is taken from the text.
relationships.display_finding: Removing the error caused substantial logit-difference drops at layers 0, 7, and 8 and high KL divergence at layers 9–11, making these SAEs insufficient for circuit analysis.

source_check.reason: Layers 0,7,8 reduce logit difference; later layers have high output KL despite increased logit difference. The corresponding groups are insufficient for analysis, preventing a complete IOI feature circuit.

relationships.condition: GPT-2 Small IOI, attention-output SAEs at layers 1–6 and groups {2,4}, {5,6}; L5 error-term ablation
relationships.reason: Splicing preserves roughly clean logit difference at layers 1–6 (r3–r8, r15, r16). Zero-ablating the L5 error term shifts logit difference by only -0.048 versus -0.826 for the top feature (r1). Whether the error matters depends on layer.
relationships.display_finding: Reconstruction retained approximately the clean logit difference at layers 1–6, and layer-5 error ablation shifted it by only −0.048 versus −0.826 for the top feature.
